title: The cap a per-owner queue count is measured against: the queue capacity or the member's personal capacity
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-011 v1, section 8 BR6 and section 12 GET /queues; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3, T3.1 queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007) and queue_member.capacity (DF-WRK-048); FSD P3 Case and workflow v4, A2.6 AC-ALT-P3-006-02
section: 8. Business rules BR6; 11. Data; 12.1 REST operations provided (GET /queues)
description: The legacy story measures every owner of a queue against one queue-level cap, while the target model gives the queue a capacity_cap and the member a personal capacity, and the FSD works an example in which one member of a queue holds a capacity of 40. No source says which of the two feeds atCap on the queue answer, or which one wins when both are set.
evidence: BR6: "An owner at or above the queue's caseload cap is shown at cap", source "Queue field capacity_cap; DL23"; AC2: "each owner in MTG-BKK-CO shows their open case count against the cap of 150"; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 queue_member DF-WRK-048 capacity, integer, optional; FSD P3 v4 AC-ALT-P3-006-02: "member U-11 of queue TDR-BKK-CO has capacity 40 and holds 40 open cases"
owner_role: Product owner for queue and caseload rules
proposed: Fix the cap in force per queue as a rule of the queue reference data: read queue.capacity_cap when the queue sets one, otherwise queue_member.capacity; until that rule is settled the app story reads queue.capacity_cap, which is the cap AC2 fixes at 150.

title: The queue summary fields, their types, and whether the summary is read live or from the queue_measure snapshot
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-011 v1, section 12 GET /queues; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3, T3.1 queue_measure (DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030); FSD P3 Case and workflow v4, A2.18 FEAT-CWC-18 and A2.39 FEAT-WKM-02
section: 11. Data; 12.1 REST operations provided (GET /queues); 13. Solution plan
description: The legacy answer names openCaseCount, oldestEntryDate, oldestAgeDays, breachCount and owners[] with ownerUserId, openCaseCount and atCap, and types none of them. The target table that holds queue measures names different things (depth, unassigned, avg_age_days, max_age_days, owner_min, owner_max, breached, status) and is a reconciled snapshot published on a schedule, while the legacy screen is a live read that must equal the case list count at the moment it is read (AC11). No source says whether the team queue answer is computed from the case rows or read from the snapshot, nor the physical type and length of each field.
evidence: Legacy section 12: "200 Queue[] with the new computed fields openCaseCount, oldestEntryDate, oldestAgeDays, breachCount, owners[] (ownerUserId, openCaseCount, atCap)"; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 queue_measure: DF-RPT-023 depth, DF-RPT-025 avg_age_days, DF-RPT-026 max_age_days, DF-RPT-029 breached, DF-RPT-030 status; FSD P3 v4 A2.18: "publishes them to the case list and Power BI"
proposed: Type the answer as openCaseCount and breachCount integers, oldestAgeDays integer, oldestEntryDate a date and owners[] with an integer openCaseCount and a boolean atCap; compute the five fields live from recovery_case and the open timer of each case, and read queue_measure only as a reconciliation check until the queue-measure story settles which one is in force.

title: The freshness answer, the X-Data-As-Of header and the value of the product placeholder in the stale banner
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-011 v1, section 12 GET /cases and section 14 MSG-P1-001; Ownership Map v1 api row GET /data-products/freshness (P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 15, rwb-source-data contract "GET /freshness (business date)"
section: 4. Flow, step 4; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 14. Validation and messages
description: The legacy story carries the business date of the case data in an X-Data-As-Of response header of the list and names a product in MSG-P1-001. In the target the freshness fact belongs to rwb-source-data, whose path is /data-products/freshness in the Ownership Map and /freshness on the architecture slides, and no source says whether rwb-case sets the header from that answer or the composite route composes the banner, nor what the {product} placeholder names on a case list.
evidence: Legacy section 12: "header X-Data-As-Of with the business date of the case data"; MSG-P1-001: "{product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived."; Ownership Map v1: "GET /data-products/freshness" owned by P1; Architecture v5 slide 14: "REST GET /freshness (business date)"
proposed: rwb-case reads the business date from GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness, caches it for the request and the business date, sets X-Data-As-Of on the two case answers and omits the header when the answer does not arrive inside the budget; the composite route renders the banner and fills {product} with the data product name the screen shows.
